title: What No Longer Comes Up
logline: Years after giving up a trade everyone locally remembers, a shopkeeper sells something else on the same street, past the same old customers, and talks plainly about the difference between holding back and not being pulled at all.

object.note: Object 10 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The weed that will not return becomes a pull that no longer comes: a shopkeeper who gave up an old trade and talks about not being pulled at all.

thread_out.thread: Freedom from an old pull leaves a mind that is simply ready: a lifeguard crew drilling the same response for a danger that may never come.

requirements: A person willing to speak openly about a past trade or habit and a real current change
Full, ongoing consent, with the ability to stop the shoot
A community where the past is known but not weaponised against the person

suggestions.name: A small town or village
suggestions.why: This kind of quiet, local reinvention could happen almost anywhere.

lesson.in_simple_terms: Holding yourself back from something and simply no longer being pulled by it are not the same. The texts say a tendency that is only held down can return, while one cut at the root does not arise again.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: යමකින් තමන්ව වළක්වා ගැනීමත්, එයට තවදුරටත් ඇදී නොයාමත් එකක් නොවේ; යටපත් කළ දෙයක් නැවත මතු විය හැකි නමුත් මුලින්ම සිඳුණු දෙයක් නැවත නූපදී.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts distinguish three ways a harmful tendency can be abandoned: held down for a while by concentration (vikkhambhana), displaced moment by moment by its opposite (tadaṅga), or cut off by path knowledge so that it does not arise again (samuccheda). Only the third is lasting; the first two support it. The texts define the stages of the noble persons (ariya-puggala) by what each path has cut off, not by rank or achievement, and a single path moment does its work once.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The film follows the shopkeeper's present work day to day, in the same street, past old customers who still mention the past. When the old trade is raised or offered, the camera simply watches how they respond. Their own unprompted account of the difference between holding back and not being pulled at all carries the film as testimony, not as a verdict.

key_terms.en: abandoning by suppression / by the opposite factor (temporary) / by cutting off

lesson.caution: The film makes no claim that the shopkeeper has reached any noble stage or had a path moment; the texts define these by inner abandoning that nothing filmed can show, and never as a ranking of people.
lesson.builds_on: The weed dug out at the root becomes a human question: what does it look like, from outside and in a person's own words, when an old pull no longer comes?
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
